sections.html:
Colorado's capital sits in the South Platte valley on the plains side of the Front Range. Its 2020 census population was 715,522, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 740,613. Denver is also a county, merged since 1902, which means a single government handles assessing, taxing and recording. Sellers deal with fewer offices than they would in most of the state.

Renters outnumber owners. Only 48.8% of homes are owner-occupied across 335,428 households (2020 to 2024). The median owner-occupied value is $616,000 and median gross rent is $1,831. Many sales here involve a landlord, an heir or someone who bought a rental and wants out. As for the median, it describes the city as a whole. A particular house can price well away from it, depending on condition, neighborhood and lot.

For Denver roofs, hail is the weather problem that costs the most. Denver is 10th among U.S. cities of 50,000 or more for hail proneness, and three of the ten costliest hailstorms in the country struck here. Snowfall averages 53.5 inches a year, July highs average 89.9 degrees, and the record of 105 degrees was set June 28, 2018.

A beaten-up roof, split siding or an insurance claim that was never repaired can stall a conventional sale, since a buyer's lender and inspector examine roofs closely. Be ready for these questions:

  • Did anyone file a claim for the hail damage, and was the work done, or was it left?
  • How old is the roof, and will a new owner's insurer cover it?
  • Have sun and freeze-thaw cycles marked the stucco, deck or paint?

Documents help. A buyer paying cash can also take the house with the damage included.

Taxes in Denver come due after the year they cover, and the Treasury Division collects them.

Payment optionDue date
First installmentLast day of February
Second installmentJune 15
Single full paymentApril 30

Weekend and holiday deadlines roll to the next business day. Statements live online. Look up your address in the property search tool, open Tax Documents and download the year you need. Paying by credit or debit card adds a 2.5% service fee, and an electronic check carries none. You can reach Treasury at 720-913-9300.

Closing agents typically split the current year's taxes between seller and buyer. Treasury also produces a Certificate of Taxes Due for Real Property, the paper a title company relies on to see what a parcel owes. Prior-year balances have to be paid before the transfer can be clean. On appeals and assessment timing, the Denver Treasury property tax page is the place to start.

sections.h2: The state fee on a Denver deed
sections.html: When a deed transfers property for more than $500, Colorado adds a documentary fee of $0.01 per $100, as county recording pages explain. Denver files deeds through the same county system. Look for that fee, the recording charge and any transfer forms on your settlement statement. Choosing a cash buyer leaves these items alone, but it can shorten the wait between signing and recording because no lender has to release loan funds.

Every short-term rental in Denver needs a license, and it must be the host's own primary residence. The business license number goes in each ad, and violators risk fines or losing the license.

That bites if you own a second Denver property that was running as an Airbnb. With the primary-residence rule, a house its owner does not live in cannot lawfully operate as a short-term rental. It may need to be sold or switched to a long-term lease, and a buyer counting on nightly income may offer less. Read the city's rental, zoning and licensing pages for your address before you list or take an offer.

Jobs in government, hospitals, schools and aviation keep demand strong near downtown. They offer no protection against a layoff, a divorce or an inherited house nobody wants to run. Events like those, more than the market, push Denver owners toward quick sales.

Inherited a house? Collect the documents showing who has authority to sign, and ask the title company what it needs before it books a closing. Own a rental with a tenant in place? Learn early whether a buyer will take it occupied. Cash buyers often do.

sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Denver house
sections.html:
Owners usually pick between an agent listing, a sale on their own and a cash purchase, and each swaps price for time and effort.

  • Agent listing: often the best price for a house in good shape, though you wait through showings, repair requests after the inspection and the buyer's loan approval.
  • Sale on your own: you keep the commission and take on the pricing, disclosures and paperwork.
  • Cash sale: the buyer takes the house as it stands, so no repair list exists and you can frequently choose the closing day.

Cash fits deferred maintenance, hail damage, a tenant in place or an estate that must be settled. A listing fits a clean house and a roomy calendar. Compare both before you decide. Our cash offer comes with no obligation.

sections.h2: Steps in a Denver cash sale
sections.html:
1. Send the address and describe the house.
  2. We review it and return a written offer.
  3. After you accept, a title company searches the record, requests the Certificate of Taxes Due from Treasury and drafts the deed.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded and the money is yours.

Set the offer beside a listing first if you like. Saying no costs nothing. Keep your tax statement close, since the property search tool lets you download it in a few minutes.

faqs.q: How much is the median home worth in Denver?
faqs.a: The 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes is $616,000. Individual houses vary widely with condition, neighborhood and lot size, so use it as a citywide benchmark.

faqs.q: When are Denver property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay in two installments, on the last day of February and June 15, or make one payment by April 30. A deadline on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Denver house that was used as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Yes. Denver requires a license and a primary-residence host, so a house that lacked either may raise compliance questions from a buyer. A cash buyer can purchase it as it stands, though you should settle any city fines or unpaid taxes.

faqs.q: Does hail damage stop me from selling a house in Denver?
faqs.a: No. Denver is among the most hail-prone large cities, so buyers expect to see it. A damaged roof can lower the price or complicate financing, which is why many owners consider an as-is cash sale.

faqs.q: What is the state documentary fee in Colorado?
faqs.a: It is $0.01 per $100 of consideration on a deed over $500, as county recording pages describe it. Look for it on the settlement statement.
